scores.notes: This has the strongest emotional arc. Using daylight as the clock is memorable, the field 'lying down' into the map is the best single image of all three concepts, and the shared day.min value keeps every number in sync. It costs too much to build: 8 sky layers, swinging shadows, digit motion-blur, a FLIP of the header icon and about 2,800vh of scroll. That is not a one-day build with high polish. The atmosphere also slows the 30-second read for a farm owner. Truth practices are good: the story numbers are reconciled and the pay is labeled as an example. It still shows dollar figures, though, and invents an invite-code format.

The paper-versus-glass contrast is warm, and the traveling punch card is a clever progress meter and table of contents. But the paper world pulls attention away from the product. Build-time rough.js and d3-contour art, the punch-clock SVG and the mobile bottom stub add work and risk. It drifts from the brief in three ways: pace changed to 48 an hour, an invented 'press and hold' note gesture, and a 'paper was the problem' story that implies things about a real farm. Ideas worth keeping: no pins on mobile, a hands-on 'Try it' map, and pay masked everywhere.

This is the clearest and most product-first concept. One phone, one shift, from a dark stage into a light paper report. Its numbers add up while keeping the brief's 34 an hour and 8 hours 30 minutes. Reduced-motion visitors never download GSAP, and a Pause motion toggle covers the ticking timers. The risky parts are the dock from a centered hero, the 3D side-turn for the Action button, the three-phone fan, a full Control Center recreation and three ScrollTrigger pins. It also invents a 'Log' tab, an invite expiry and a $15/hour example rate.

decision:
WINNER: 'Gloves On'. Its spine stays: one lit iPhone carries one Friday shift, voice first, the lock screen second, the map breaks out into a full-bleed field, and the lights come up for the paper time card. It wins on clarity, which matters most for a farm owner reading for 30 seconds. It also has the best accessibility and performance posture.

CUT FROM IT to make a one-day build with high polish:
- The hero-to-slot dock. The phone starts in its slot.
- The 3D side-turn. The Action button and Control Center become one small static 'Controls' card.
- The three-phone fan. Crew uses two overlapping phones.
- All ScrollTrigger pins. Every hold is CSS position: sticky inside a tall track, so there are no pin spacers, CLS stays 0, and iOS Safari behaves.
- The invented Log tab, the invite expiry and the $15/hour rate.

GRAFTED FROM 'First Light, Last Row':
- One shared DayClock value (day.min) drives the status-bar time, the Live Activity timer, the shift ribbon and the header mark, so time and visuals cannot drift.
- The app icon becomes a live clock in the header: the cream fir hand rotates with the story's time.
- A cheap version of the day's color script: one stage tint per section, crossfaded by opacity, instead of 8 sky layers.
- A dawn horizon of fir-row silhouettes in the hero, built from the icon's own three-tier tree.
- The field 'lies down' from a horizon perspective into the flat map, with gold rows pouring in.
- Karaoke-style spoken lines, odometer numbers and the paper 'printing' row by row.
- The 'Sharpening shears' break with a reason, and the dictated shift note.

GRAFTED FROM 'Punched & Penciled':
- A hands-on 'Try it' map strip that works with or without motion.
- The struck-through ghost 'Clock out' button beside the lock screen.
- Pay masked on every screen (no dollar figures anywhere on the page), which also demonstrates hide-pay.
- A play-on-enter mobile approach where pinning would fight the phone.
- Static-first DOM: the SSR markup is the final state, and JS only adds from-states.

ONE LEDGER: Every number on the page comes from site/src/data/ledger.ts, and Vitest checks the arithmetic. It reconciles the brief's sample lines:
- 7:02 in, 4:31 out, 59 minutes of breaks, 8 hours 30 minutes worked.
- 34 an hour and 290 trees.
- 212 trees at 2:01 PM on row 35.
- 'Row 12 was shaped by Sam on Oct 16.', used verbatim.
title: Gloves On: one phone, one shift
tagline: Keep your gloves on. A time card for Christmas tree trimmers that runs on your voice and your lock screen.
metaDescription: Time Card is an iPhone time card for people who shape Christmas trees. Clock in, mark rows and take lunch by voice or from the lock screen. Open source, in development, TestFlight beta coming.
concept:
The page is a product film you scroll through. One iPhone, lit like a studio shot on a deep fir-green stage, carries one trimmer through one Friday on the farm (Friday, October 16), from “Clock in with Time Card” at 7:02 AM to a clean paper time card after 4:31 PM.

Each section shows a feature at the hour a trimmer would use it:
- the voice commands through the morning and lunch
- the big lock-screen Live Activity at 2:14 PM
- the whole field of 8,540 trees
- a break with tree notes
- the crew and offline sync at the back of the field
- pace at 3:40 PM
- clock-out and the weekly report

The feeling runs from 'tapping a phone in gloves is a pain' to 'I didn't think about the phone all day'.

The light tells the day:
- cool dawn in the hero
- deep and focused for the lock screen
- warm afternoon for pace
- dusk at clock-out
- the lights come up for the paper report, and the page stays light for the honest closing

The copy is plain and short and written for trimmers first, owners second and developers last. The page never claims more than exists today: in development, TestFlight beta coming, open source on GitHub.
scrollDevice:
ONE PHONE, ONE SHIFT, ONE CLOCK.

1) DAYCLOCK (src/scripts/dayclock.ts)
- A single shared object, day = { min: 422 }, holds minutes after midnight (422 = 7:02 AM).
- Every section's scrubbed timeline tweens day.min (ease 'none') between that section's ledger times, alongside its own screen animation.
- A gsap.ticker callback runs only when day.min has changed. It updates four things:
  (a) every visible status-bar clock (h:mm, no AM/PM, as on iOS)
  (b) every visible Live Activity timer, via ledger.workedAt(min) or breakAt(min), formatted h:mm:ss with odometer digits
  (c) the shift ribbon fill and time tag
  (d) the header DayMark hand rotation
- Scrolling back rewinds the day.
- After scrolling stops, the visible timer ticks in real time for up to 5 seconds, then rests.
- The Pause motion toggle stops all of this ticking (WCAG 2.2.2).

2) SHIFT RIBBON (in the sticky header)
- A 3px bar under the 56px header fills from 7:02 AM (0%) to 4:31 PM (100%) as a scaleX transform on a fir-to-gold gradient.
- A small Plex Mono tag rides its leading edge: '7:02 AM · Clock in', '7:18 AM · Say it', '2:14 PM · Lock screen', '2:15 PM · The field', '2:30 PM · Break', '2:47 PM · The crew', '3:40 PM · Pace', '4:31 PM · Clock out', 'End of shift'.
- Desktop (≥900px): nine tick marks sit on the ribbon. Each is a real <a href='#id'> inside <nav aria-label='The shift'>, labeled on hover and focus. This doubles as keyboard section navigation.
- Mobile: the tag is a <button aria-expanded> that opens the same list as a disclosure panel under the header.

3) DAYMARK
- The header's 28px app icon is a live clock: a deep-green rounded square, a gold ring and a cream fir tree as the hand.
- The hand rotates with day.min on a 12-hour dial: 7:02 = 211deg, noon = 360deg, 4:31 = 495.5deg.
- The gold ring arc fills from 7 AM to the current time (stroke-dashoffset).

4) THE STAGE PHONE (desktop ≥900px wide and ≥560px tall, motion allowed)
- One fixed, aria-hidden phone frame sits in the right column (columns 7–12, vertically centered, height min(78svh, 760px)).
- Each section owns its screen layers in its own static <figure>. When a section becomes active (ScrollTrigger onToggle on its track), stage.ts moves that section's screen-layer container into the stage phone's screen slot (appendChild), then moves it back when the section is left.
- The section's own figure becomes visually hidden; its figcaption stays readable by screen readers.
- Between sections the screen swap is a 0.35s crossfade plus a specular sheen sweep, so it reads as one phone through the whole day.
- Mobile (<900px), reduced motion and no-JS: nothing is moved. Each section shows its own phone, sticky inside the section on mobile with motion, and static inline otherwise.
- Scene code is identical in both cases, because it targets ctx.phone (the stage frame or the section frame) and ctx.screens (the same nodes).

5) HOLDS
- There are no ScrollTrigger pins.
- Every section is a tall track (heights per section) that contains a 100svh position: sticky frame.
- Each section's timeline uses start 'top top', end 'bottom bottom', scrub 0.6, and is normalized to duration 1, so every spec below reads in progress units 0–1.
- Native scroll is never hijacked, and there is no snapping.

designSystem.layoutGrid:
Mobile first. Breakpoints are 600, 900 and 1200px.

MOBILE (<900px):
- One column with 16px side gutters.
- Header 56px plus the 3px ribbon.
- Section phones are height min(52svh, 460px), sticky at top: 68px.
- Copy cards (--card-dark, radius 20px, padding 20px) scroll up over the lower 30% of the phone. Each card is spaced so its beat plays while it sits in the lower 45% of the viewport.
- No horizontal scroll at 320px or wider. Wrappers use overflow: clip and nothing is wider than 100vw.

DESKTOP (≥900px):
- 12 columns, max content width 1240px, 24px gutters, centered.
- Copy lives in columns 1–5 (max 34rem). The stage phone slot is columns 7–12, centered, height min(78svh, 760px), width = height × 393/852.
- stage.ts writes the slot rect into --stage-x, --stage-y, --stage-w and --stage-h on :root, so section-local extras (second phone, callouts, paper) can align to it.
- Full-bleed breakouts: the field map and the paper report.

PHONE SCREENS:
- Authored in a 393×852pt space with container units: .screen { container-type: inline-size } and --pt: calc(100cqw / 393).
- Every in-screen size is calc(N * var(--pt)), so a phone is crisp at 200px or 900px wide.

VERTICAL RHYTHM: 8px base. Section tracks are measured in vh and svh as specified per section.
designSystem.motion:
'Like a well-made tool: confident, short, no wobble.' GSAP 3.15 core, ScrollTrigger, SplitText and Flip, all from npm. No MotionPathPlugin: packet dots use SVG getPointAtLength.

1) Only transform, opacity, clip-path and stroke-dashoffset animate. Glows, sheens and shadows are pre-baked layers whose opacity changes. Nothing animates layout, box-shadow, filter or backdrop-filter.

2) Scrubbed section timelines use scrub 0.6 with ease 'none' on time and camera moves. Inside them, discrete UI events (taps, sheets) are short nested tweens with iOS-like eases.

3) Taps (helper tap()):
- A 44pt touch ring scales .6 to 1.4 while its opacity goes .35 to 0.
- The target presses to scale .94, then releases with back.out(1.8).
- The phone does a 2px x 'haptic' shake over 2 cycles.
- Each tap takes about .04 of progress.

4) Screen changes:
- The outgoing layer goes to scale .96 and opacity 0; the incoming layer comes in from scale 1.04.
- Unlock: the lock layer moves to yPercent -100 while the app layer scales .94 to 1.
- Sheets: yPercent 100 to 0.
- A specular sheen (a 20deg band of 12% white, opacity only) sweeps on each change.

5) Numbers never jump. Odometer digit columns roll by yPercent and snap to integers.

6) Headlines: SplitText lines mask-reveal (yPercent 100 to 0, stagger .08, .7s, power3.out). They are triggered once at 'top 75%', not scrubbed. The hero H1 is never hidden.

7) Spoken lines use karaoke: words go from opacity .25 to 1, scrubbed. Siri replies reveal by word on the page and type in the phone.

8) Callouts draw a 1px gold leader line (stroke-dashoffset), then the label slides 8px and fades in.

9) Stage tints crossfade over .8s, triggered by section.

10) Ambient loops (ticking timers, Siri glow breathing) run only during scroll plus 5 seconds after, and never while Pause motion is on.

11) gsap.matchMedia contexts:
- 'desk': (min-width: 900px) and (min-height: 560px) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference); uses the stage.
- 'mob': (max-width: 899px) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference); section phones.

12) ScrollTrigger.config({ ignoreMobileResize: true }). ScrollTrigger.refresh() runs after document.fonts.ready and on a ResizeObserver of <main>.
designSystem.reducedMotion:
With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce (or no JS, or JS failure), GSAP is never downloaded.

An inline <head> script adds html.motion only when motion is allowed and innerHeight is at least 560. Every from-state lives under .motion selectors. A 4-second safety timeout removes .motion if the scene bundle has not booted.

Without .motion:
- Section tracks collapse to natural height, and no sticky frames are used.
- Each section shows its static final-state figure(s) inline, with visible figcaptions.
- Multi-state sections show 2–3 small labeled figures as specified per section.
- Timers show fixed ledger values.
- The ribbon fill and time tag are hidden. The chapter links remain as a plain nav list.
- The DayMark is static at 7 o'clock (the app icon as designed).
- Stage tints are painted as each section's own static background gradient.
- Spoken lines and Siri replies are plain static transcript bubbles.
- The Try it map still works, with instant state changes.
- Pause motion is hidden because nothing moves.
designSystem.imagery: No photography, no stock, no people and no real farm. Scenery is drawn from the product. The hero has fir-row silhouettes, all built from one (the app icon's three-tier rounded tree). The field map is 8,540 dots on Canvas 2D. The report is the paper time card. The app icon is inline SVG (cream fir as the hand of a gold clock ring on deep green), plus a 180px apple-touch PNG and favicon.svg. The iPhone frame is pure CSS: - 393×852pt proportions with a corner radius of 55pt. - A brushed-titanium edge from layered gradients, 1px inner highlight, black bezel. - Dynamic Island 126×37pt at y 11pt, and side buttons including the Action button. - No Apple logo. The frame has a gold rim-light layer and a soft elliptical contact shadow (a pre-blurred element). Status bar, tab bar and control glyphs are custom inline SVG; SF Symbols are never used. The lock-screen wallpaper is an SVG of dawn fir rows, plus one pre-blurred WebP twin (393×852 @2x, 12 KB or less) behind the Live Activity material. REAL CAPTURES: Screen.astro checks at build time (fs.existsSync) for site/public/screens/.{avif,webp,png} at 1179×2556. When one exists, it renders in place of the HTML recreation, using the same alt text.

sharedComponents.name: SectionShell (src/components/SectionShell.astro)
sharedComponents.purpose: A consistent wrapper so parallel teams only write content and a scene.
sharedComponents.spec:
PROPS: id, navLabel, ribbonTag, eyebrow, headline (H2), tint (stage-tint key), track ({ desk: '260vh', mob: '220vh' }), theme ('dark' | 'light').

RENDERS
- <section id aria-labelledby='{id}-h' data-tint data-theme style='--track-desk; --track-mob'>.
- Inside: .track (height var(--track-*) only under html.motion) > .frame (position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh under motion) holding the slots copy, figure and extras.
- Slot 'figure' holds the section's <figure class='shot'>: the Phone with its screen layers, plus a <figcaption> that is visible without motion and sr-only with motion.
- Copy beats are <div class='beat' data-beat='n'>. On desktop they stack in columns 1–5 and are placed at fixed progress positions with CSS top percentages inside the track. On mobile they are cards in the flow after the sticky figure.

SCENE REGISTRATION
- The section's scene file is src/scripts/scenes/{id}.ts and calls registerScene(id, build).
- build(ctx) receives ctx = { tl, phone, screens, extras, day, isDesk, util }:
  - tl: a scrubbed timeline normalized to duration 1.
  - phone: the stage frame on desktop, or the section frame on mobile.
  - screens: the section's layer container.
  - day: day.to(tl, minute, from, to).
  - util: tap, odometer, karaoke, typeIn, drawLine, crossfade, sheen, callout.

CONTRACT
- The phone frame transform must be at rest ({ x: 0, y: 0, scale: 1, rotation: 0, opacity: 1 }) at progress 0 and 1.
- Screen layers must end in the state the next section starts from, as listed in that section's spec.
- Text reveals never start below opacity .2 unless they are triggered on enter.

sharedComponents.purpose: The 8,540-dot map used in the field section, the crew screens and the Try it strip.
sharedComponents.spec:
LAYOUT
- A small TypeScript port of the field geometry: blocks in 2 rows × 7.
- Each block is 10 dots wide and 61 rows tall. Gutters are 1.5 dot-pitches between blocks and 3 pitches between the two block rows. Block labels 'Block 1'–'Block 14' in Plex Mono 11px.

- Canvas 2D with DPR capped at 2.
- Dot sprites (ring, earlier, today, note flag) are pre-rendered once to offscreen canvases and drawn with drawImage.
- The full overview is pre-rendered to one offscreen bitmap. Updates redraw only the rows that changed.
- Zoomed views redraw per rAF with setTransform and cull dots outside the viewport.
- Redraw happens only when progress changes. The module initializes only within one viewport of its section (IntersectionObserver, rootMargin 100%).
- A ResizeObserver handles size.

ACCESSIBILITY
- The canvas has role='img' and an aria-label built from the ledger: 'Map of North field: 14 blocks of 61 rows, 10 trees a row, 8,540 trees. Rows 14 to 36 of block 2 shaped today in gold. Block 1, blocks 8 and 9, and the first rows of blocks 2, 3 and 4 shaped earlier in green. The rest not yet shaped.'

sharedComponents.name: Motion core (src/scripts/motion.ts, stage.ts, dayclock.ts, util.ts)
sharedComponents.purpose: Shared boot, gating and helpers so scenes stay small.
sharedComponents.spec:
BOOT
- An inline head script sets html.motion when (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) matches, innerHeight is 560 or more, and navigator.connection?.saveData is not true.
- main.ts loads as type=module, deferred. Only if html.motion is set does it dynamic-import gsap, ScrollTrigger, SplitText, Flip and the scenes.
- A 4-second safety timeout removes .motion if booting fails.

GSAP SETUP
- gsap.matchMedia sets up the 'desk' and 'mob' contexts. Each builds scenes for sections lazily, when the section is within 1.5 viewports (IntersectionObserver).

stage.ts (desk only)
- Creates the fixed stage phone and two tint layers.
- claim(section) moves screen layers in; release(section) moves them back.
- Writes --stage-* rect variables on resize.
- On claim it runs a .35s crossfade and a sheen.

dayclock.ts
- The day object, a ticker that updates [data-clock], [data-timer] and the ribbon, a 5-second idle real-time tick, and Pause support.

util.ts
- tap(tl, el, at)
- odometer(tl, el, from, to, at, dur, format)
- karaoke(tl, el, at, dur)
- typeIn(tl, el, at, dur)
- drawLine(tl, path, at, dur)
- crossfade(tl, a, b, at, dur)
- sheen(tl, at)
- callout(tl, {line, label}, at)

A focusin listener scrolls the focused element's beat into view, so a keyboard user never lands on content that is still faded.

sections.headline: Keep your gloves on.
sections.body: Time Card is an iPhone time card for people who shape Christmas trees. Clock in, mark your rows and take lunch by voice, with your phone locked in your pocket. The lock screen does the rest.

Primary button: Follow along on GitHub (https://github.com/joshmiller83/treefarm-timecard)
Secondary link: Walk through a shift ↓ (#voice)
Fine print: Open source, MIT licensed. Not on the App Store yet.
Spoken line above the phone: “Clock in with Time Card.”
Siri reply in the phone snippet: “Clocked in at 7:02. You're on block 2, row 14.”

sections.goal: Prove that voice is the main way to work. Use real phrases and short answers, with the phone locked in a pocket or through AirPods. Show the misheard-number check, lunch, and asking for stats, including the pay privacy rule.
sections.headline: Say it. Keep cutting.
sections.body: Every command has the app's name in it, so Siri knows where it goes. It works with your phone locked in your pocket, or through AirPods. The answers are short, so you're back on the shears fast.
bullets: 7:18 AM. You: “Mark row fourteen in Time Card.” Siri: “Row 40 in block 2? That's 26 rows ahead.” You: “No.” Caption: Far-off rows get a double check, in case Siri heard forty for fourteen. Nothing changes until you say yes.

7:19 AM. You: “Next row in Time Card.” Siri: “Row 14 marked, 10 trees. Next is row 15.” Caption: It marks the next row you haven't done and moves you on. When the block changes, it says the block out loud.
12:01 PM. You: “Take lunch with Time Card.” Caption: The lock screen turns gold and a lunch timer starts. Your worked time stops right where it was.
12:31 PM. You: “Back to work with Time Card.” Siri: “Back at 12:31. Lunch was 30 minutes.”

2:01 PM. You: “How many trees in Time Card?” Siri: “212 trees today, 34 an hour. You're on block 2, row 35.” Caption: Ask about hours, pace or pay too. On a locked phone, Siri only says your pay out loud if you allow it.
Chip row, labeled 'More to say:' “Undo in Time Card” · “Add a note in Time Card” · “Note a tree in Time Card” · “Clock out with Time Card”

sections.headline: Your time card, right on the lock screen.

sections.goal: Close honestly and warmly: where it came from (a working tree farm in Indiana, unnamed), the status (in development, TestFlight beta coming, not on the App Store), open source MIT, the stack for developers, and one clear call to action, GitHub. The footer is included.
sections.headline: Built on a working tree farm. Out in the open.
sections.body:
Time Card grew out of a simple web time card used on a working Christmas tree farm in Indiana. The iPhone app is the next step.

It's in active development. A TestFlight beta is coming. Nothing is on the App Store yet.

The code is open source under the MIT license. It's Swift all the way through: a SwiftUI app that works with Siri through App Intents and puts your timer on the lock screen with ActivityKit, plus a small Vapor and SQLite server your farm runs itself. Ours runs on a Mac at home behind a Cloudflare Tunnel. Every rule is written test-first.

TARGETS: Lighthouse mobile ≥ 90 for performance (asserted in CI), accessibility ≥ 95, best practices ≥ 95, SEO ≥ 95.

BYTES (gzipped)
- HTML: 75 KB or less. The screens are light DOM, and repeated SVG uses <symbol>/<use>.
- CSS: 35 KB or less, inlined by Astro where small.
- JS:
  - First-load JS is 6 KB or less: the head gate, header disclosure, Try it and the dayclock stub.
  - Motion bundle loaded on demand: 80 KB or less. That is gsap core plus ScrollTrigger, SplitText and Flip (about 50 KB), plus scenes, stage, dayclock, fieldmap and util (30 KB or less).
  - Reduced-motion visitors download none of the motion bundle.
- Fonts: 120 KB or less, two preloaded.
- Images: the blurred wallpaper WebP (12 KB or less) and og.png (social only). Everything else is SVG or CSS.

TIMINGS (Moto G Power, slow 4G profile)
- LCP is the hero H1 text, under 2.5s.
- CLS under 0.02: fixed aspect-ratio phones, metric-matched font fallbacks, and sticky instead of pin spacers.
- TBT under 200ms: the motion bundle is imported after first paint with requestIdleCallback, and scenes are built lazily per section.
- INP under 200ms.

RUNTIME RULES
- Animate only transform, opacity, clip-path and stroke-dashoffset. The one exception is the single color transition at the lights-up.
- No live filter or backdrop-filter. Set will-change only during active tweens.
- At most 2 tint layers are visible at once.
- The field canvas uses DPR 2 at most, redraws only on progress change, culls when zoomed and initializes near the viewport.
- The DayClock ticker does nothing when day.min is unchanged. Ambient loops stop 5s after scroll and on Pause.
- content-visibility: auto on sections more than one viewport away, in reduced-motion mode only.
- No third-party requests, analytics, cookies or trackers.
accessibility:
STRUCTURE
- A skip link comes first ('Skip to content', targeting <main id='content'>).
- Landmarks: header, nav 'The shift', main, one <section aria-labelledby> per chapter, and footer.
- Heading order: one H1 in the hero, an H2 per section, and an H3 for the report sub-beat.
- All copy is server-rendered in reading order that matches the visual order.

MOCKUPS
- Each phone root is role='img' with a concise aria-label from the section spec. Everything inside is aria-hidden.
- Each <figure> has a figcaption: visible without motion, sr-only with motion.
- The stage phone is aria-hidden; its information already lives in the section figures.
- Live timers are aria-hidden next to static text.
- The report is a real table. The field canvas has a role='img' summary.
- Spoken lines are marked up as <q> or <blockquote> with 'You' and 'Siri' labels in text.

KEYBOARD
- Every interactive element is a real <a> or <button> with a target of 44px or more.
- Focus ring: 3px solid #E2A644 on dark and #1D5B3A on light, with a 2px offset, never removed.
- The ribbon chapter links and the mobile disclosure (aria-expanded) work by keyboard.
- Try it is a role='grid' with roving tabindex and a polite live region.
- Pause motion is a toggle button with aria-pressed.
- A focusin listener scrolls the focused element's beat into view.
- Nothing traps focus. Scroll is never hijacked: Space, Page Down, anchors and find-in-page all work.

MOTION
- prefers-reduced-motion gets a complete, composed static page with no GSAP.
- No loop runs longer than 5 seconds without user scroll, and Pause stops all ambient motion (WCAG 2.2.2).
- No flashing.
- Text reveals never leave focusable text invisible.

COLOR
- Every text pair is checked against AA, as listed in the design system colors.
- Gold text on light only at 24px bold or larger.
- Map states differ by size and lightness as well as hue.

TESTING
- axe-core in Playwright at 375 and 1440, in motion and reduced modes.
- A manual VoiceOver pass on iOS Safari and macOS Safari before launch.
truthRules:
1. STATUS: In active development. A TestFlight beta is coming. Nothing is on the App Store. Say this in the hero pill, the header pill and the closing section. Never write 'download', 'available', 'get it', 'launching', a date, a price, or any App Store or Google Play badge or styling.

2. NO SOCIAL PROOF: no invented testimonials, quotes from users, ratings, download, user, farm or star counts, press logos, or 'trusted by'.

3. NO REAL FARM OR PEOPLE: never name, picture or describe the real farm beyond 'a working Christmas tree farm in Indiana'. Example people are Alex, Sam and Rosa only. 'North field' is fictional. Sanitize any strings copied from the original web time card, whose source title contains the farm name. No email address anywhere.

4. FEATURES: only features in the product description appear. Specifically, do not show:
- invite code formats or expiry
- a Log tab
- long-press note gestures
- a clock-out button on the lock screen
- pay on the report
- anything about Android or iPad

The tab bar uses Clock, Trees, Report and Team pending confirmation.

5. NUMBERS: every number comes from ledger.ts and is example data from one illustrative shift. The sample Siri replies keep the product's phrase formats but use ledger numbers so the day adds up (8 hours 30 minutes, 290 trees, 34 an hour). No dollar figures anywhere; pay is shown hidden.

6. SIRI WORDING: lines not given in the product doc are flagged verified: false in siri.ts and must be confirmed against the App Intents dialog strings before launch, or replaced. These are the misheard confirmation, 'Noted on row 36, tree 7.' and 'Added to today's notes.' The 'Take lunch' reply is deliberately not shown.

7. SCREENS: the HTML screens are recreations of the app as it's being built. The footer says so, and real simulator captures replace them via site/public/screens/ when available.

8. PLATFORM QUALIFIERS: Action button on iPhones that have one; Control Center controls need iOS 18 or later; a Live Activity lasts up to 8 hours and the app reminds you before then.

9. TRADEMARKS: Apple names are used factually. No Apple logo. The trademark line goes in the footer. The Siri glow and the iPhone frame are generic recreations.

10. DEVELOPER CLAIMS: the stack, test-first, MIT and the Mac plus Cloudflare Tunnel hosting are as described. Never claim test counts or coverage. The terminal command renders only if CI finds it in the README.
